jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in Mississippi, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in Mississippi, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it, and who represents you there — county, Mississippi Senate, Mississippi House and U.S. House districts, cities, towns and villages, school districts and ZIP codes.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 4 congressional districts — the largest districts Mississippi carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 4 features for Mississippi, measured 2026-10-15. Mississippi did not redraw for 2026: the 120th-Congress map and the 119th's (layer 4) carry the same four districts with identical land areas.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Mississippi Senate District
layers.rank_note: 52 Senate districts — larger on average than a county, smaller than a congressional district

source.answers: The Mississippi Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (state upper chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 52 features, measured 2026-10-15. These are the lines of the 2025 court-ordered redraw, which moved nine Senate districts (1, 2, 11, 19, 34, 41, 42, 44 and 45) for the special elections of 4 November 2025. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 20 m interval and refused over a 25 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: ms-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Mississippi Legislature's own member gallery and each member's own profile (name, party, Senate e-mail address and the Senate's Capitol office). The gallery shows a vacant seat as a card reading Vacant, and the card says so: Senate 34 on 2026-10-15. The profiles also print a home address, a personal telephone and sometimes a personal e-mail address, and the builder never reads them.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 82 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

source.answers: Which county contains the point, and the five supervisors on its board.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 82 features, measured 2026-10-15.

source.people: ms-county-officials.json, rebuilt weekly: the five members of each county's board of supervisors, by district, from the Mississippi Secretary of State's County Offices and Directory (2026 edition, published 6 May 2026). The board's address and telephone are carried only where at least three of the five supervisors print the same one, because five people do not share a home: 76 counties have a board address and 68 a board telephone on the 2026 edition. A supervisor's own address or telephone is never carried, and neither is anything the directory prints for the election commissioners.

layers.label: Mississippi House District
layers.rank_note: 122 House districts — smaller on average than a county, larger than a school district

source.answers: The Mississippi House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (state lower chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 122 features, measured 2026-10-15. These are the lines of the 2025 court-ordered redraw, which moved five House districts (16, 22, 36, 39 and 41). Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 20 m interval and refused over a 25 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: ms-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Mississippi Legislature's own pages on the same terms as the Senate roster; House 70 and 77 read vacant on 2026-10-15.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 137 unified (K-12) districts covering the whole state, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file)

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), queried live at runtime; 137 features for Mississippi, measured 2026-10-15.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD NAMES THE DISTRICT ONLY. Mississippi's school boards are elected in most districts and appointed in some, and no statewide roster of their members has been read here. Recorded as gap ms-school-board-members.
source.applies: Mississippi — statewide. The label carries no qualifier because there is nothing to distinguish it from: the elementary and secondary tilings TIGERweb serves for other states are EMPTY in Mississippi (0 features each, measured 2026-10-15), and the 137 unified districts' Census land area sums to exactly the 82-county total (121,535 km2).

layers.label: County Supervisor District
layers.rank_note: 410 supervisor districts statewide, five per county, about 296 km2 of land on average against 887 km2 for a school district; drawn only in the counties whose current lines are confirmed

source.answers: Which of the county's five supervisors represents the point, in the counties where this app has confirmed the current district lines. The layer is hidden in the other counties, where the County card still names all five.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — tigerWMS_Current, layer 22 (County Subdivisions, January 1, 2026 vintage), where the Census files each supervisor district as a nonfunctioning county subdivision; pre-built and shipped with the app for the 12 counties whose lines the Census changed after the 2020 census and whose five districts hold nearly equal numbers of people on that census's own blocks (3.2% to 9.0% apart, measured 2026-10-15): Choctaw, Clay, DeSoto, Grenada, Lawrence, Lowndes, Neshoba, Noxubee, Oktibbeha, Tate, Webster and Winston. Elsewhere the Census still carries the lines drawn after the 2010 census, which are not drawn.

source.people: ms-county-officials.json, the roster the County card reads: the supervisor elected from each district, from the Mississippi Secretary of State's County Offices and Directory (2026 edition, published 6 May 2026), joined by district number.
source.applies: 12 of Mississippi's 82 counties; hidden in the other 70, which the Data gaps panel lists and explains.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 827 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas in the state's own bounding box, fetched live by envelope; the layer hides outside Mississippi

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, queried live at runtime. ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='28'. 827 features in Mississippi's box, measured 2026-10-15.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Mississippi. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code (the Alabama test point gives 36925).

source.answers: The city, town or village containing the point, if any.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), queried live at runtime; 300 features for Mississippi (113 cities, 167 towns and 20 villages, one of the towns recorded by the Census as inactive), measured 2026-10-15.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Mississippi's cities, towns and villages elect a mayor and a board of aldermen or a council, and no statewide roster was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap ms-municipal-officeholders.
source.applies: Mississippi — statewide. A point outside every city, town and village is unincorporated, which the card states.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-10-15: 462 points in Mississippi's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap today, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Mississippi — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: the State Capitol, Jackson, Hinds County

negative_point.note: near York, Sumter County, ALABAMA, about 12 km east of the Mississippi line — outside Mississippi and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-10-15: TIGERweb's county layer names Sumter County, Alabama at this point (control: the Capitol anchor returns Hinds County, Mississippi), and the Census's ZIP layer answers 36925 there, which is the neighbouring-state answer the ZIP layer's coverage test exists to hide. ALABAMA BECAUSE NO INSTANCE SERVES IT and it is not on the next-states list; Louisiana, Arkansas and Tennessee, which share Mississippi's other borders, were passed over so this point does not have to move when any of them is live.
